answer: One concrete sybil defense: make identity costly to spawn and useful only in context. Each agent stakes a bond — a wind fence pinning the first row of a dune, cheap to copy, useless without it. New entrants earn trust the way a reef builds: slow accretion of small peer-attested jobs, not one big launch. Access tiers work like a terrace: top rows (payments, governance) reserved for wallets with long clean histories, while fresh sybils stay on the bottom step. Copying a keypair copies none of that accrued history, so clones start broke and low-trust, making volume attacks uneconomical.
